lessons.title: Perfekt
lessons.summary: The spoken past: haben or sein + past participle at the end. This is how Germans tell what happened.

cards.title: When do you use it?
cards.body: Whenever you talk about the past in conversation, messages and postcards: your weekend, your holiday, what you did yesterday. **Ich habe in Rom Pizza gegessen.** **Wir sind ans Meer gefahren.**

examples.english: At the weekend I read a lot.

cards.title: haben/sein + participle
cards.body: **haben** or **sein** at position 2, the **past participle** at the end. Most verbs use **haben**. Verbs of **movement from A to B** (fahren, gehen, fliegen, kommen) and **change** (aufstehen, einschlafen) use **sein** — plus **sein** and **bleiben** themselves.

cards.title: Regular participles: ge-…-t
cards.body: Regular verbs: **ge** + stem + **t**. Stem in -t/-d: ge…**et**. Verbs in **-ieren**: no ge-.

cards.title: Irregular participles: ge-…-en
cards.body: Irregular verbs end in **-en** and often change their vowel. Learn them with the verb. Separable verbs put **ge** in the middle: auf**ge**standen. Inseparable verbs (be-, ver-) have no ge-: **besucht**, **vergessen**.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'Ich habe gefahren': movement takes **sein** — **Ich bin gefahren**. Don't put the participle in the middle: **Ich habe gestern Tennis gespielt**, not 'Ich habe gespielt gestern Tennis'.

games.explanation: Movement, change, sein and bleiben → sein; the rest → haben.
No ge- for be- verbs and -ieren verbs.

games.english: Yesterday I went to the cinema.
games.explanation: gehen is movement: ich bin gegangen.

lessons.topic: Simple past of some verbs (einige Verben im Präteritum)
lessons.title: war, hatte, konnte…
lessons.summary: For sein, haben and the modal verbs Germans prefer the simple past, even when speaking: Ich war in Berlin.

cards.title: When do you use it?
cards.body: Telling about a trip or your weekend: **Wie war der Urlaub? – Er war super!** With **sein**, **haben**, **es gibt** and **modal verbs** the simple past (Präteritum) sounds more natural than the Perfekt.

examples.german: Das Hotel **war** schön, aber wir **hatten** kein Glück mit dem Wetter.
examples.english: The hotel was nice, but we had no luck with the weather.

cards.title: sein and haben
cards.body: Learn these two tables: ich and er/sie/es are the **same** and have no ending.

cards.title: es gab = there was
cards.body: **es gibt** (there is) becomes **es gab** (there was/were) — with the accusative, as in the present.

examples.english: There was no pool at the hotel.

cards.title: Modal verbs: -te
cards.body: Modals add **-te** and lose the umlaut: **konnte, musste, durfte, wollte, sollte**. For **möchten** use **wollte**.

examples.english: We had to wait a long time.

cards.tip: No umlaut in the past: können → konnte, müssen → musste.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'ich habe gewesen': **ich war** (or ich bin gewesen). Not 'ich musste gehe': the infinitive goes to the end — **ich musste gehen**. Not 'konnte' with umlaut.

games.explanation: These verbs prefer the simple past.
The subject is euer Urlaub (er): war.

lessons.title: nach, in, zu, aus…
lessons.summary: Where to, where and where from: nach Berlin, in der Stadt, zum Bahnhof, aus Italien.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Travelling and telling about it: **Ich fahre nach Wien.** **Ich wohne im Hotel.** **Ich komme aus Italien.** **Wir gehen zum Strand.** Three questions: **Wohin? Wo? Woher?**

examples.english: In summer we're flying to Spain.

cards.title: Wohin? (where to)
cards.body: **nach** + cities, countries without article, **nach Hause**. **in** + countries with article and places you enter (**in die Schweiz, ins Kino**). **zu** + people and places/buildings (**zum Arzt, zur Bank**).

cards.title: Wo? and Woher?
cards.body: **Wo?** **in** (in Berlin, im Hotel), **bei** + people (bei meiner Oma), **zu Hause**. **Woher?** **aus** + cities, countries, buildings; **von** + people and places (vom Arzt).
cards.tip: zu, bei, von, aus are always followed by the dative: zum, zur, beim, vom.

cards.title: Short forms
cards.body: Preposition + article melt together: **zu dem → zum**, **zu der → zur**, **bei dem → beim**, **von dem → vom**, **in dem → im**, **in das → ins**.

examples.german: Ich gehe **zur** Post und dann **ins** Café.
examples.english: I'm going to the post office and then to the café.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'zu Berlin': **nach Berlin**. Not 'nach Hause' for 'at home': that's **zu Hause**. Not 'Ich gehe nach dem Arzt': **zum Arzt**.

games.explanation: nach/zu → where to, in/bei → where, aus/von → where from.
